source.title: Beyond Superficial Forgetting: Thorough Unlearning through Knowledge Density Estimation and Block Re-insertion
source.authors: Feng Guo; Yun-Tao Wen; Shen Gao; Jun-Shuo Zhang; Shuo Shang

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present. Some appendix figure text is garbled in the extraction; the main tables and prose are readable.
record.tranche_reason: The study tests whether RTT fine-tuning can recover forgotten knowledge, using multiple unlearning methods, models, and datasets, and evaluates a new counter-method. It is a conceptual test of recovery and robustness rather than a direct replication of the claim’s cited methods as a whole.
record.gate_note: The paper reports RTT results for several unlearning methods and a prefix-injection result for GD and KUnBR. It lists nine prompt-attack variants, but reports a numerical outcome only for Prefix Injection; the other attack names alone are not rows. It argues that cover layers mask residual knowledge, but does not directly ablate an activation direction. No quantization experiment is reported.
record.test_reason: Table 1 applies the RTT relearning attack (fine-tune on subset T, test on disjoint V) to GA, GD, RMU, RIA, NPO and the new KUnBR on two models and four datasets. This bears on A and B for existing methods and on F for KUnBR. One prompt attack (Prefix Injection) is quantified, which bears weakly on E. The cover-layer account (C) is asserted, not tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that standard methods (GA, GD, RMU, RIA, NPO) leave residual knowledge that RTT recovers, and attribute this to 'cover layers' without testing it. They claim KUnBR forgets more thoroughly, resists RTT and prompt attacks, and preserves utility. Their prompt-attack claim rests on a single Prefix Injection number.
record.recipe_differences: KUnBR is a new block-reinsertion method using Gradient Difference as a warm-up and again on selected blocks. RTT fine-tunes on a subset T of the forget set. It is not a reproduction of the cited unlearning recipes.
record.method_sensitivity: Recovery varies by model and dataset; the paper also reports different forgetting outcomes across block-selection strategies and block-count/Top-K settings, but the extracted Table 4 layout does not support reliable assignment of all values.
record.problems: No uncertainty estimates are reported. Recovery is not compared with a model that never saw the target knowledge. The prompt-attack result is quantified only for Prefix Injection, and its model and exact comparison baseline are not stated. Table 2 does not identify the model for its utility scores or give an unlearned-model reference. Some appendix figure/table extraction is garbled.
record.rows_left_out: Table 1 baseline forget and post-RTT accuracy rows, plus recovery rows for RIA and NPO, were omitted to stay within the 60-row limit; Table 1 is the locator. Comparator results from Table 2 were also omitted. Table 4's block-count/Top-K results were not extracted because the flattened layout does not reliably assign several values; the paper reports these in Table 4. Other listed prompt variants have no separately stated outcomes. The Table 3 method ablations do not directly test the claim's recovery attacks.

untested.parts: No comparison of recovery against a model that never saw the knowledge. Baseline forget and general-ability values are from Table 1/2 text, not rows.
Relearning on unrelated or loosely related data is not tested; only the forget-set subset T is used.
Not tested. Cover layers are an asserted explanation; there is no direction ablation or probing.
Eight of nine listed prompt attacks have no reported outcome, including cross-lingual and in-context.
KUnBR is not tested against quantization, activation ablation, or unrelated-data relearning.

missing.what: The Table 1 block-to-model mapping is ambiguous in the extraction; the text's claims fit the first block being LLaMA. Rows labelled Z and L may be swapped, along with their original-accuracy baselines.
Case study: GA, GD, RIA and NPO recall the forgotten answer after RTT; KUnBR does not (qualitative, single example).

record.verdict_notes: KUnBR is the authors' own counter-method, and the main evidence for F is the authors' own evaluation. There are no error bars and no never-exposed control. Some reported accuracies are below 4-choice chance (e.g., 16.5, and 18.18% on WMDP), which complicates reading 'recovery'. Several RTT accuracies exceed the stated original accuracy (e.g., 66.8 vs 65.6 on WMDP), which suggests table inconsistencies. The claim 'confirms genuine knowledge removal' near Table 4 is not backed by a removal-vs-access test.

versions.untested_parts: Tests forgetting accuracy, utility metrics, RTT, and a prefix-injection result, but not all simple attacks. It does not compare recovery with a model that never saw the knowledge.
The recovery attack fine-tunes on a subset T of the forget set. Unrelated or loosely related examples are not tested.
No activation-direction ablation or direct internal-access-versus-deletion test is reported. Cover layers are proposed as an explanation.
Only Prefix Injection has a reported outcome. Other languages, jailbreaks, rephrasing, and the other listed prompt variants are not separately quantified.
Tests KUnBR against RTT and reports a Prefix Injection outcome; it does not test quantization or activation-direction ablation.

relation.reason: Table 1 reports RTT recovery for the baselines and for KUnBR, which bears on A, B and F. The prefix attack bears weakly on E.

tranche.reason: KUnBR is a new method on the same question, evaluated with Deeb and Roger's RTT protocol (same datasets and split ratios). The baseline re-runs come close to T1 for B, but the study is a method paper.

source_check.notes: Table 1 is flattened; Zephyr-first block order is inferred from label order. Against it: Zephyr post-RTT then exceeds its stated originals (WMDP 66.8 vs 59.2, Years 68.3 vs 56.3), and the LLaMA 'smallest increase' claim fits block 1 better. Prefix attack: 1 of 9 attacks quantified; model and n unstated.

statements.correction: GA/GD/RMU recovery in Table 1 runs 7.01-63.7. 18 of 23 cells fall in 22.3-63.7. The cells below 20 are Zephyr GD RB 15.3 and, on LLaMA, GD RB 14.0, GD MMLU 14.0, RMU RB 7.64 and RMU MMLU 7.01. GA LLaMA RB is a dash. GA Zephyr RB goes 23.5 -> 87.2 (63.7). RTT trains on T and is scored on the disjoint V.
statements.problem: The GAZ_RB numbers are right, but '20-64 points' for GA, GD and RMU leaves out 5 of the 23 cells, which recover less than 20.

statements.correction: LLaMA block, against originals of 99.3 (RB) and 54.7 (MMLU): GD RB 32.5 -> 46.5 (14.0), RMU RB 46.5 -> 54.1 (7.64), GD MMLU 34.4 -> 48.4 (14.0), RMU MMLU 47.8 -> 54.8 (7.01). The authors attribute the low Rec of some baselines, e.g. RMU on MMLU, to limited forgetting.
statements.problem: Recovery numbers are right, but the cited RB cells are not shallow forgetting: LLaMA RB falls from 99.3 to 32.5 (GD) and 46.5 (RMU), yet recovers only 14.0 and 7.64. GD MMLU's 14 points bring it to 48.4 of 54.7. The ranges don't pair: forget '48' matches only RMU MMLU (47.8), whose recovery is 7.01, below the stated 7.6. The authors' limited-forgetting explanation is given for RMU on MMLU, not for these cells.

statements.correction: Table 1 has one hyperparameter setting per method. LLaMA GD RB goes 32.5 -> 46.5 (14.0). Table 3 only ablates KUnBR components (re-insertion, pre-unlearning), and Table 4 varies KUnBR's block count and Top-K on Years.
statements.problem: The study never varies unlearning depth, duration or learning rate for any method. GDL_RB_REC is a single cell at one setting.

statements.correction: KUnBR is tested only with RTT (fine-tune on forget subset T, score on disjoint V) on Zephyr-7B-beta and LLaMA3-8B-Instruct. Post-RTT accuracy is 28.0 (Zephyr MMLU) and 28.5 (LLaMA Years), and 34.4-47.1 in the other six cells. The study has no benign or out-of-domain fine-tuning.
statements.problem: The cited KUnBR rows come from RTT on a forget-set subset, scored on Years and MMLU. The statement's conditions are benign, unrelated or out-of-domain fine-tuning on WMDP Bio/Chem/Cyber. The two cited cells are the only near-chance ones of eight.

statements.correction: KUnBR recovers 7.0-20.4 points, with post-RTT accuracy 34.4-47.1 in six cells and 28.0/28.5 in two. Its post-RTT accuracy is lowest in 7 of 8 cells (LLaMA RB: GD 46.5, KUnBR 47.1). Some baselines recover fewer points: Zephyr NPO RB 7.0 and MMLU 7.6; LLaMA RMU RB 7.64 and MMLU 7.01. Datasets: RB, WMDP-Deduped, Years, MMLU.
statements.problem: KUnBR stays above chance after RTT in the six cited cells. But it recovers 7.0-20.4 points, 12-45% of the accuracy lost, which is not clearly 'a large share'. Only WMDP-Deduped is a hazardous-knowledge set, and the models are not Llama-3.1-8B. Several baseline cells recover fewer points.
